Every pallet, verified.
Every order, ready to ship.

The Outbound Checklist prepares an order for shipment. The operator verifies every pallet while packing it, and the app produces the one consolidated sheet that travels with the delivery — in place of an Excel that only ever compared quantities and part numbers.

01 · Today

The Excel sheet checks two things: do quantities and part numbers match.

The operator scans the barcode on every box of every pallet, in sequence, and the sheet compares that count and part number against the order's pick label. That's all it validates.

Quality control

Won't let an incomplete report print

If a field is missing, if the quantities don't match, if the height exceeds the destination's maximum, or if the box's part number was never verified, the app blocks printing — and marks in red exactly what's missing and on which pallet.

Spot-check

Pull any box off any pallet and check it.

Every box in an order has to carry the same part number. At any point during packing, the operator can open the random audit, walk to whichever boxes they like — on one pallet or across several — and scan them. Each scan is checked against the order’s part number, or against the first box scanned when the order’s PN isn’t in yet. A part number that doesn’t belong surfaces on the spot, instead of at the customer.

Result

One report. Everything together.

Destination, pallet type, weight, height, part-number verification and quantities — in a single document, printed and clipped straight into the shipment packet. Nothing left to assemble by hand afterward.

The shipment packet

Four documents, one metal clip.

Verifying pallets is only half the job. What actually leaves with the order is a packet — clipped together in the same order every time. The app changes exactly one sheet in it.

HMCG94AGBRA
EP · 288 kg · 142 cm
Pick label 12.8 × 6.3 cm · sheets A4
  1. 01 Pick label(s)12.8 × 6.3 cm · one per pallet Pallet type, weight and height are written on it by hand — the only place those three values exist.
  2. 02 The printed ExcelA4 Quantities and part numbers, and nothing else. Every other field had to be collected from somewhere else.
  3. 03 Packing listA4 Goes in third, unchanged.
  4. 04 WBO — Warehouse Delivery OrderA4 Closes the packet, unchanged.
The clip, the order and the packet stay exactly as they are. One sheet changes — and that sheet now arrives already verified, with nothing left to write in by hand and nothing left to go looking for.

For Security & IT

Everything stays on the device.

Built to operate inside the warehouse, without opening up any new attack surface.

No internet connection required
Doesn't need a network to work. Scanning, calculation and validation all happen on the device.
No installation
It's a single file. Opens with a double-click on any PC — no deployment, no IT involvement needed.
Nothing leaves the device
Delivery data is never sent to a server or to the cloud. It's stored only in that machine's browser.
Minimal attack surface
No backend, no remote database, no login to compromise. There's no server to attack.
Isolated multi-session
Multiple deliveries in parallel, each one independent. No session can read another one's data.
No third-party credentials
Doesn't rely on any account, external login or identity service to operate.
In detail: the app loads two visual resources over the internet if a network is available (a typeface and a library used only for PDF export) — with no connection, it keeps working exactly the same, minus that visual detail.
How it's built

Deliberately simple.

Nothing to maintain, nothing to break.

A single file
Everything — screen, logic and styling — lives in one .html file. No installer, no infrastructure dependencies, no server to maintain.
Runs in the browser
Any PC in the packing area, in the browser that is already on it. Opening the file is the entire "setup".
Saves on the device
Each delivery is an independent session, saved locally. You can have more than one delivery open at once, in separate tabs.
Validates before printing
A mandatory check blocks the report if anything is missing or doesn't match — it doesn't rely on the operator remembering to check.

Compatible with the Zebra DS3678 scanner

The operator scans exactly as always — the reader connects over Bluetooth in HID Keyboard Wedge mode, so to the app it's indistinguishable from someone typing. Every Enter (or Tab, depending on how the reader is configured) is accepted the same way: a beep and a green flash confirm the read.

If a scan doesn't make sense — a purchase-order code instead of a quantity, for example — the app rejects it instantly with a red alert, before the error ever reaches the report.

In summary

Scanning a box didn't change. Everything else did.
